{{nihongo|'''Tago Shrine'''|哆胡神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in Tago, {{ill|Nishiizu|Q1203949|qid=Q1203949}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Shizuoka|Q961511|qid=Q961511}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}<ref>[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4401179 哆胡神社] - Shizuoka Prefectural Shrine Office</ref>. {{nihongo|'''Tago Shrine'''|哆胡神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

== Overview ==
It is enshrined in the center of the Tago district, on high ground (Ainoura) just south of Ōtago Beach.

Its founding is unknown, but it is an old shrine identified with the similarly named {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} Tago Shrine (たごじんじゃ), and is also recorded in the ''{{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}'' as "Junior Fourth Rank Upper, Tago no Myōjin"<ref name="gen">[https://genbu.net/data/izu/tago_title.htm 哆胡神社] - Genbu</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140309-01.html 多胡神社] - Study of Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

In 1873 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was listed as a village shrine<ref name="engi"/>.

Originally it stood in the northern Ōtago district as Hachiman Shrine, but in 1881 ({{ill|1881|Q7808|qid=Q7808}}, Meiji 14) it was merged with Mishima Shrine of the southern Itago district and moved to its present location<ref name="engi"/>.

* Tago Wakamiya-no-Mikoto
